info.title: Agendor API
info.description:
# Introduction

Welcome to our API docs! Agendor is a CRM system made to streamline the
sales process of teams of inside and outside sales. With our API, you
can integrate your existing systems with Agendor and make your sales
team even more efficient. Check out some help articles our team has
written about integrating with our API (in Portuguese):

* [Do you have examples of how to use the Agendor API?](https://ajuda.agendor.com.br/integracoes/voces-tem-exemplos-de-como-utilizar-a-api-do-agendor)
* [Can I integrate Agendor to my current system?](https://ajuda.agendor.com.br/integracoes/o-agendor-pode-ser-integrado-ao-meu-sistema-atual)

## Structure

Our API is a RESTful JSON API, which means:

* The endpoints are structured around *resources*, identified by URIs;
* HTTP *verbs* are used to act differently on the same resource
and HTTP *status codes* are used to signal the result of an operation;
* We expect body parameters in JSON and also respond in JSON.

The body of succesful responses will have up to three main root level
properties:

* `data`: actual data of the resource you're working with, will always
be present;
* `meta`: metadata about the resource, for instance total size of a
collection of results;
* `links`: links to related resources, which can be used to navigate
through the API.

The failure responses will be signaled by HTTP status codes and also
have error details under the `errors` property in the response body.

## Authentication

<!-- ReDoc-Inject: <security-definitions> -->

To authenticate your requests, you need an API token. You can find
your token by logging into Agendor, and going to
[Menu > Integrações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/integracoes).
This token is like your password, so keep it secret!

Add this token to the `Authorization` header of your requests, using
the `Token` scheme, for example, in cURL:

```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Token your-token-here' https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/users/me
```

In PHP, you might do:

```php
$curl = curl_init();

curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, array("Authorization: Token your-token-here"));
curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_URL, "https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/users/me");

$response = curl_exec($curl);
```

In case of failed authentication, the API will respond with a `401`
status code and the following body:

```json
{
  "errors": [
    "Token could not be authenticated"
  ]
}
```

If you're getting this error, you might be using an invalid token or
your headers are not set up properly. Check if your Agendor account and
user are active and if you have included your token in the `Authorization`
header, preceded by the word `Token`.

## Pagination

In the endpoints where you might `GET` a collection of resources, they
will be paginated. By default, `10` items are returned per page, but
you can increase the page size up to `100`.

To navigate through the results, use the `page` parameter, starting
from page `1`. The total count of results will be included in the
`meta` property of the response and links for the following and
preceding pages will be  included under `links`:

```bash
GET https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/organizations?page=2

{
  "data": [...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "totalCount": 100
  },
  "links": {
    "self": "https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/organizations?page=2",
    "prev": "https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/organizations?page=1",
    "next": "https://api.agendor.com.br/v3/organizations?page=3"
  }
}
```

## Webhooks

Webhooks let your system be notified when something happens in Agendor.
Subscribe a URL to an event and Agendor will send a `POST` with a JSON
body to that URL every time the event happens.

Subscriptions are managed at `https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions`,
using the same `Authorization: Token your-token-here` header.

Available events: `on_organization_created`, `on_organization_updated`,
`on_organization_deleted`, `on_person_created`, `on_person_updated`,
`on_person_deleted`, `on_deal_created`, `on_deal_updated`,
`on_deal_deleted`, `on_deal_won`, `on_deal_lost`, `on_deal_stage_updated`,
`on_activity_created`, `on_activity_updated`, `on_activity_finished`,
`on_activity_deleted`, `on_product_created`, `on_product_updated` and
`on_product_deleted`.

Each delivery has the following body:

```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "actionUser": { ... },
  "triggeredAt": "..."
}
```

### Managing subscriptions

```bash
# Create a subscription
POST https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions
{ "target_url": "https://example.com/webhook", "event": "on_deal_won" }

# List your subscriptions (optionally filtered by ?event=on_deal_won)
GET https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions

# Remove a subscription
DELETE https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions/:id
```

### Authenticating deliveries

You can register one authentication header per subscription. Agendor
sends it in every delivery, so your endpoint can check that the request
came from Agendor. Send `auth_header_name` and `auth_header_value`
when creating the subscription:

```bash
POST https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions
{
  "target_url": "https://example.com/webhook",
  "event": "on_deal_won",
  "auth_header_name": "X-Webhook-Token",
  "auth_header_value": "your-secret"
}
```

To set, replace or remove the header of an existing subscription, use
`PATCH`. Both keys are required; send `null` in both to remove the
header. The `target_url` and the `event` are never changed by this
request.

```bash
PATCH https://api.agendor.com.br/integrations/subscriptions/:id
{ "auth_header_name": "X-Webhook-Token", "auth_header_value": "new-secret" }
```

Rules (an invalid header returns `422`):

* Name and value must be sent together;
* Name: a valid HTTP header name, ASCII, up to 64 characters. `Host`,
`Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding`,
`Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `TE`, `Trailer`,
`Upgrade`, `Expect`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Proxy-Connection` and
`Cookie` are not allowed;
* Value: printable ASCII, up to 1024 bytes, without leading or trailing
spaces and without line breaks.

The value is never returned by the API: responses include only
`auth_header_name`.

The header is read when each delivery is sent, so a change also
applies to deliveries that are waiting to be retried.

**Register the header in Agendor before requiring it in your
endpoint.** Deliveries answered with `401`, `403` or `404` are
considered delivered and are not retried, so requiring the header first
makes you lose events.

### Delivery

* `410`: the subscription is removed;
* `5xx` and connection errors: retried, and the subscription is removed
when the retries are exhausted;
* Any other status (including `401`, `403` and `404`): considered
delivered and not retried.

tags.name: organizations
tags.description:
Organizations are other businesses that you sell to; in other
words, your B2B customers. If you sell B2C, you might want to use
[people](#tag/people) instead.

Use these endpoints to add new organizations, search for and update
existing organizations, or remove them.

tags.name: custom_fields
tags.description:
Custom fields are custom areas for including additional information on organizations, people and deals.

Use this endpoint to verify all custom fields added to your records.

tags.name: people
tags.description:
People are your contacts, either with an [organization](#tag/organizations),
if you sell B2B, or your actual customers if you sell B2C.

Use these endpoints to add new people, search for and update existing
people, or remove them.

tags.name: deals
tags.description:
Deals are your business opportunities. You can create deals associated
with [organizations](#tag/organizations), if you sell B2B,
or to [people](#tag/people), if you sell B2C.

Use these endpoints to create new deals (always under a organization
or person), update their info, [stage](#tag/deal_stages) and
[status](#tag/deal_statuses), search for specific deals, or remove them.

tags.name: tasks
tags.description:
Tasks represent small units of work that you have to perform in
order to find opportunities or advance them through your funnel.
They always have to be associated with a customer, either
[organization](#tag/organizations) or [person](#tag/people), or a
[deal](#tag/deals).

Use these endpoints to create, update, find or delete tasks.

tags.name: users
tags.description:
Users are the members of your team that add more customers, perform
tasks and win deals.

Use these endpoints to list your users and update them.

tags.name: categories
tags.description:
Categories are a way to segment your customers to find and identify
them more easily.

You can configure your categories in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

tags.name: sectors
tags.description:
Sectors are a way to indicate what business segments your customers
work with.

You can configure the relevant sectors for your account in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

tags.name: products
tags.description:
Use products to discriminate *what* you're selling in each deal or for
each customer.

You can configure your portfolio of products through these endpoints or in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

tags.name: lead_origins
tags.description:
Lead origins represent what channels your customers came from.

You can configure your available lead origins in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

tags.name: loss_reasons
tags.description:
Loss reasons are the causes that you have identified of why you might
lose a deal.

You can configure your available loss reasons in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

tags.name: metrics
tags.description:
Metrics are tags that you can attach to tasks to be able to measure
later.

You can create and configure your metrics in
[Menu > Relatórios > Métricas](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/relatorios/criar.php).

tags.name: funnels
tags.description:
Funnels are the different processes that your deals might go
through.

To configure funnels in your account, please contact our Customer
Support team.

tags.name: deal_stages
tags.description:
Ongoing deals will be advancing through your sales funnel, each step
closer to being won. The deal stages represent these steps that your
deals go through in your funnel.

You can configure the stages of your own sales process in
[Menu > Configurações](https://web.agendor.com.br/sistema/configuracoes).

get.description:
Lists and searches for tasks using the available filters. Date bounds are inclusive.
Requests without any of `entityType`, `entityId`, `includeRelatedEntity`, `includeDeals`,
`assignedUserIds`, `createdByUserId`, `finishedByUserId`, `metricIds`, `withAttachments`,
`indexed=true`, `typesIn`, `dateField`, `excludePinned`, `sortBy` or `sortOrder` must include
at least one of `dueDateGt`, `finishedDateGt`, `updatedDateGt` or `createdDateGt`.
Each lower bound must be within 31 calendar days of its upper bound (or today when no
upper bound is supplied). With any of the listed filters, date bounds may be provided
independently.

**Filters:** `entityType` and `entityId` must be supplied together. Different filters
are combined with AND; IDs within `assignedUserIds` or `metricIds`, and values within
`typesIn`, are combined with OR. If both `metricId` and `metricIds` are supplied,
both constraints must match. `finishedEq` filters completion in both search modes.
`indexed=true` selects indexed search without adding a filter. Omitting it or sending
`indexed=false` keeps the legacy path when no new filter is present. `dateField=due_at`
requires a due date; other dateField values are not supported. Results are limited to
activities the authenticated user is allowed to access. Without `sortBy`, indexed
results are ordered by creation descending, then update ascending. With
`sortBy` (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `dueDate` or `finishedAt`), `sortOrder` accepts
`asc` (default) or `desc`. Missing dates are placed last in either direction.
Records with the same sort value have no guaranteed relative order.
sortOrder without sortBy returns 400. dateField filters date presence independently
of sorting. Omitting both sorting parameters uses the default ordering.
`meta.totalCount` contains the total number of matching tasks when available.
Pagination links keep their existing format.

**Pagination limit:** indexed search only reaches the first 10,000 matching tasks.
A page beyond that returns 422, and the `next` link is omitted on the last reachable
page. `meta.totalCount` still reports the full total. To reach more tasks, narrow the
date filters and paginate each range separately.

parameters.name: withAttachments
parameters.description: Filters activities by whether they have attachments.

parameters.name: indexed
parameters.description: Selects indexed search when true, without adding a filter. Defaults to false; new filters still select indexed search.

parameters.name: typesIn
parameters.description: Activity types, combined with OR. Notes have no metrics or due date; generic tasks have a due date and no metrics. Other types match the corresponding account metric; an unconfigured type has no matches.

parameters.name: dateField
parameters.description: Requires a due date to be present. Does not change ordering or require a date range.

parameters.name: excludePinned
parameters.description: Excludes active pins for the requested entity before pagination. Defaults to false; has no effect without an entity.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Date used to sort results. Missing dates are last; equal values have no guaranteed order.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: Sort direction. Requires sortBy; defaults to asc only when sortBy is supplied.

parameters.name: includeVoip
parameters.description: Includes audioTranscription and audioSummary when available. Defaults to false.

lossReason.description:
Loss reason for the deal. Only accepted when the deal's status is (or is being set to) 'lost'.

Example: `{ "id": 1, "description": "Customer chose a competitor" }`

Fields:
- `id` (integer): Loss reason ID (from GET /v3/loss_reasons).
- `description` (string, optional): Specific description for this deal's loss.

relatedEntity.description:
Replaces the organization or person linked to this deal. The previous link is
cleared automatically — a deal can only be linked to one entity at a time.

Example: `{ "type": "person", "id": 123 }`

Fields:
- `type` (string): Either 'person' or 'organization'.
- `id` (integer): ID of the person or organization, which must be visible to the current user.
